D1_rationale: Era-based natural experiment (2003-2005 discontinue vs 2006-2009 continue) is vulnerable to secular-trend confounding, comorbidities such as diabetes and prior SSI were not collected, and PsA is only ~4-5% of the pooled rheumatic cohort and is not isolated in any outcome model.
D2_rationale: All rheumatic patients undergoing elective orthopedic/hand surgery in the window were enrolled with follow-up starting at surgery, but group assignment by calendar era introduces mild time-based selection.
D3_rationale: The continue-vs-discontinue exposure is defined by a dated, ethics-committee-approved institutional policy change (no. 229/2006) with drug regimens recorded contemporaneously in a clinical database, independent of outcome.
D4_rationale: The perioperative discontinuation/continuation protocol and standardized antibiotic prophylaxis were applied uniformly by era, though individual adherence to the policy around each procedure was not separately verified.
D5_rationale: Missing data were minimal - 33 procedures (2.1%) lost to follow-up and 29 (1.8%) missing drug data were excluded and characterized, leaving near-complete (~98%) follow-up.
D6_rationale: SSI was ascertained per 1992 CDC definitions and classified by a single author unblinded to era, and the authors note these definitions are not validated for elective arthroplasty.
D7_rationale: Pre-specified a priori covariates, multiple regression models, and sensitivity analyses are transparently reported including null findings, with no registered protocol available.
Overall_rationale: Serious risk driven by confounding (secular-trend era design, uncollected comorbidities, non-isolated trace PsA subgroup) despite a clean policy-defined exposure and near-complete follow-up.

D1_rationale: The stopped-versus-continued SSTI comparison is unadjusted (Fisher/chi-square only) despite confounding by indication (reason for holding often undocumented) and a mixed cohort dominated by IBD in which psoriasis/PsA are a minority and not isolated.
D2_rationale: The surgical subgroup (218 procedures/180 patients) was drawn from biologic users who underwent surgery with follow-up beginning at operation, a reasonable selection although exposure-defined subgrouping is retrospective.
D3_rationale: Held-versus-continued status was abstracted from pre- and post-operative notes, but the reason for holding was frequently not documented, allowing some exposure misclassification.
D4_rationale: Hold duration varied and was analyzed by number of drug half-lives elapsed (P=.52), with no evidence of differential co-interventions between groups.
D5_rationale: Data were retrospective and provider-documented and the reason for holding was often missing, though denominators for the primary stop/continue comparison appear complete.
D6_rationale: Postoperative SSTI was defined as provider-documented skin infection within 90 days requiring antibiotics, and the authors acknowledge that misdiagnosis of cellulitis is prevalent, risking (likely non-differential) outcome misclassification.
D7_rationale: Primary and secondary comparisons including the near-significant stop/continue SSTI difference (14.5% vs 6.3%, P=.08) are reported without evident selective reporting.
Overall_rationale: Serious risk from unadjusted confounding in the stop/continue comparison within a mixed IBD-dominated cohort where psoriasis/PsA outcomes are not isolable.

D1_rationale: Logistic regression adjusted for concomitant immunosuppression, diabetes, smoking, and prophylactic antibiotics in a clean 100% psoriasis/PsA cohort, though residual confounding by indication remains (biologics were stopped more often for major/orthopaedic surgery).
D2_rationale: All psoriasis/PsA patients on biologics undergoing a procedure over 6 years were identified from records with each procedure treated as an independent event.
D3_rationale: Continue-versus-stop status and median per-agent stop/restart days were recorded from records, providing a reasonably well-characterized exposure.
D4_rationale: Stop durations varied (some <4 half-lives) and were examined in a sensitivity analysis restricted to guideline-concordant holds.
D5_rationale: As a small retrospective audit the dataset appears complete for the main analyses, although microbiology was available for only one complication case.
D6_rationale: Complications (infection, delayed wound healing) and disease flare were provider-documented and retrospective, with flare being a partly subjective outcome.
D7_rationale: Complication and flare results plus major-surgery and half-life sub-analyses are reported, though significance tests were computed on the whole 77-procedure cohort rather than the orthopaedic subset.
Overall_rationale: Moderate risk overall - a clean psoriasis/PsA population with confounder adjustment offsets the small sample and residual confounding by surgery type/severity.

D1_rationale: Multinomial propensity-score inverse-probability weighting balanced extensive covariates (comorbidities, glucocorticoid dose, DMARDs, surgeon volume) and comparing infliximab stop-timing among users mitigates confounding by indication, though disease activity is unmeasured and PsA/PsO/AS enter only as a combined covariate.
D2_rationale: Rigorous cohort definition using validated algorithms with strict exclusions for non-elective/pre-existing infection and outcome ascertainment beginning post-operatively.
D3_rationale: Infliximab stop timing was derived from date-stamped Part B infusion claims, a best-in-class objective exposure measurement.
D4_rationale: Timing categories were well-defined, glucocorticoid co-medication was adjusted for, and restart timing was modeled as a time-varying covariate.
D5_rationale: Continuous Medicare enrollment was required and follow-up was near-complete (e.g., 3996/4288 with 90-day SSI follow-up), with minimal missingness.
D6_rationale: Serious infection used validated ICD-9 codes (PPV>80%) while the PJI code (996.66) is unvalidated, but three alternative PJI definitions yielded concordant results, implying limited (non-differential) misclassification.
D7_rationale: Two pre-specified primary outcomes, an a priori power calculation, and numerous sensitivity analyses are transparently reported.
Overall_rationale: Moderate risk - a methodologically strong propensity-weighted claims study whose residual limitations are unmeasured disease severity, an unvalidated PJI outcome, and non-isolated psoriatic disease.

D1_rationale: The review-relevant TNFi-versus-non-bDMARD comparison was not propensity-matched (matching applied only to the OA control) and the groups differ significantly in age (p<0.001), AS and RA proportions, with no disease-activity or clinical data available.
D2_rationale: Defining the perioperative-TNFi cohort by a prescription in the 6 months before AND after surgery conditions on post-operative survival/re-prescription, an immortal-time/selection concern the authors acknowledge could miss patients with early complications requiring prolonged discontinuation.
D3_rationale: Exposure is prescription pick-up (a surrogate for adherence) and the authors state they could not ascertain the actual rate or length of perioperative TNFi discontinuation, so continuation cannot be cleanly distinguished from brief holds.
D4_rationale: Institutional guidance (withdraw ~2 half-lives, resume 7-14 days post-healing) was not individually verified and roughly 30% non-adherence to prescriptions is plausible.
D5_rationale: BMI was missing in 17.3%, but the hard revision endpoint was well-captured including revisions performed outside the region.
D6_rationale: The primary outcome, implant revision for any cause, is an objective endpoint captured comprehensively (~95%) by the RIPO arthroplasty registry.
D7_rationale: Survival curves and detailed causes of revision are reported for all three cohorts; no power calculation was performed (registry-based).
Overall_rationale: Serious risk from confounding (unmatched, significantly imbalanced comparison groups without disease-activity data) and selection (exposure partly defined on post-operative prescription), despite an objective registry-captured survival outcome.

D1_rationale: Propensity-score matching (IS vs no-IS) plus multivariable regression adjusting for age, sex, BMI, smoking, procedure risk and medication class was used, but baseline disease activity (no CRP/ESR) was unmeasured and biologic use was not cleanly isolated from other immunosuppression.
D2_rationale: All baseline-IS patients contributed to the stay-versus-held subgroup analysis; the 888 no-baseline-IS patients without propensity matches were excluded, appropriate for the matched comparison.
D3_rationale: On-IS versus held-IS status and medication class were recorded from records per 2017 ACR/AAHKS timing, but the isolated 'on biologic' covariate likely codes ever-on-a-biologic rather than a clean continued-versus-held biologic contrast.
D4_rationale: Holding and restarting followed ACR/AAHKS guidance, though medication compliance was assumed and not verified (acknowledged).
D5_rationale: Flares may be under-ascertained because patients could self-manage without presenting, and compliance was not accounted for.
D6_rationale: The flare outcome was physician-diagnosed within 12 weeks, a partly subjective and potentially under-reported endpoint assessed without blinding.
D7_rationale: The primary flare outcome, multivariable regression, survival analysis, and a power calculation are all reported.
Overall_rationale: Moderate risk - a propensity-matched, adjusted design offset by unmeasured baseline disease activity, imperfect isolation of biologic exposure, and possible flare under-reporting.

D1_rationale: Only univariate chi-square/Fisher tests were used with no multivariable adjustment, and the TNFi-user-versus-non-user comparison in a single continuation-era cohort is subject to confounding by indication with very low event counts (7 PJI).
D2_rationale: All inflammatory-arthritis primary TKA/THA patients (2006-2015) were identified via ICD-9 codes and validated by chart review, with follow-up starting at surgery.
D3_rationale: Perioperative medication was abstracted from records by a single investigator in a continue-only cohort; TNFi exposure is well-recorded but there is no within-study discontinuation arm.
D4_rationale: All patients were managed under the uniform post-2006 continue-through-surgery policy, so co-intervention application was consistent.
D5_rationale: Missing data were limited (8 cases missing 1-year follow-up were resolved via record review; ASA missing in 43, BMI in 20) and did not affect the result.
D6_rationale: PJI/SSI were classified using explicit CDC/orthopaedic microbiological criteria with standardized 1-year telephone follow-up, giving a fairly objective outcome.
D7_rationale: SSI and PJI are reported across multiple subgroups including PsA-specific counts; no multivariable model was fitted owing to the low event rate.
Overall_rationale: Serious risk driven by confounding - an unadjusted, underpowered user-versus-non-user single-arm continuation cohort - though PJI outcome ascertainment is sound.

D1_rationale: Cohorts were matched on age, sex and Elixhauser index, but psoriasis severity was not adjusted and the biologic (TT/B) subgroup differs systematically (younger, higher comorbidity), leaving confounding by indication for why patients receive biologics.
D2_rationale: Psoriasis and 1:4 matched non-psoriasis lumbar-discectomy patients were drawn from a large administrative database with treatment subgroups defined by prescription records.
D3_rationale: Exposure is chronic biologic prescription rather than a perioperative continue-versus-hold decision; the authors explicitly state they could not determine if or when medications were discontinued around surgery, a fundamental mismatch with the review's perioperative construct.
D4_rationale: No perioperative medication intervention was defined or measured, so adherence to any hold/continue strategy cannot be assessed.
D5_rationale: As an administrative-claims study, comorbidity and prescription data are reasonably complete but constrained by coding accuracy.
D6_rationale: SSI and sepsis were identified from ICD codes within 90 days, subject to administrative coding accuracy but likely non-differential.
D7_rationale: SSI, sepsis, 5-year reoperation, and all four treatment-subgroup analyses are fully reported.
Overall_rationale: Serious risk because the exposure captures chronic biologic use rather than perioperative timing (D3) and psoriasis severity confounding is unaddressed, though the pure-psoriasis SSI signal remains usable as recommendation-level evidence.
